kits.familyName: Protecting information on paper, screens and in talk
setup: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}, where confidential information appears on paper, on screens and in conversation.
As {role|a} at {workplace|a}, you handle confidential information in several forms during the day.
detail: It is the middle of the afternoon.
pressure: {coworker3} says it is not worth the trouble.
You are in a hurry to finish.

tiers.1: Information anyone can see right now should be covered first.
tiers.2: Conversations can be overheard, so move before you talk.
tiers.3: Personal devices are outside the workplace's control.
tiers.4: Files in transit need a sealed, labeled cover.
tiers.5: Retired storage still holds information until it is wiped.

fact: Customer names and account numbers are still on the whiteboard after a meeting, and the policy says boards are erased before leaving.
issues.short: the information left on the whiteboard
issues.action: Erase the whiteboard before you leave the room.
issues.reason: Cleaners, visitors and other staff also use the room, and an erased board shows nothing.
issues.lesson: Cover or erase information in view before you leave a shared space.

shortcut.text: Leave it up, since only staff come into this room.
shortcut.brief: leave the board as it is
shortcut.why: Visitors and cleaners also enter, and the policy says to erase it.
shortcut.mis: Only employees ever see the room.

clear: The whiteboard was already erased after the meeting.

fact: You are on the phone about a customer's account in a public area, and the policy says to discuss accounts only in private.
issues.short: the call in the public area
issues.action: Move to a private area before continuing the call.
issues.brief: move somewhere private for the call
issues.reason: People nearby can hear details you would never show them on paper.
issues.lesson: Discuss confidential details only where others cannot overhear.

shortcut.text: Lower your voice and keep talking where you are.
shortcut.brief: lower your voice and keep talking
shortcut.why: A quiet voice can still be overheard, and the policy requires a private area.
shortcut.mis: Speaking softly is the same as speaking privately.

clear: You already moved to a private area for the call.
issues.done: the call is already in a private area

fact: You want to photograph a handwritten customer list to send to yourself, and the policy keeps confidential information off personal devices.
issues.short: the photo of the customer list
issues.action: Skip the photo and ask {lead|the} how to copy the list on an approved device.
issues.brief: skip the photo and ask about an approved copy
issues.reason: A photo on a personal phone leaves the workplace's control, even if you plan to delete it.
issues.lesson: Keep confidential information off personal devices, whatever the format.

shortcut.text: Take the photo and delete it as soon as you have used the list.
shortcut.brief: take the photo and delete it later
shortcut.why: The photo sits on a device the workplace does not control until you delete it, and the policy forbids it.
shortcut.mis: A temporary copy on a personal phone is harmless.

clear: You already deleted the photo and asked about an approved copy.

fact: Customer paper files must go to another branch, and the policy says files travel only in a sealed, labeled envelope.
issues.short: the files going to the other branch
issues.action: Seal the files in a labeled envelope before they leave.
issues.brief: seal the files in a labeled envelope
issues.reason: A sealed, labeled envelope protects the files on the way and shows where they should go.
issues.lesson: Send paper files only in the sealed, labeled cover the policy describes.

shortcut.text: Send them in an open folder so the other branch can check them quickly.
shortcut.brief: send the files in an open folder
shortcut.why: An open folder can lose pages or be read in transit, and the policy requires a sealed envelope.
shortcut.mis: Faster to open means better for the receiver.

clear: The files were already sealed in a labeled envelope.

fact: An old storage drive from your workstation is being thrown away, and the policy says retired drives go to IT for wiping.
issues.action: Give the drive to IT to be wiped instead of throwing it away.
issues.brief: give the drive to IT for wiping
issues.reason: Deleted files can often be recovered, so only a proper wipe makes retired storage safe.
issues.lesson: Hand retired storage to IT instead of throwing it out.

shortcut.text: Delete the files yourself and put the drive in the trash.
shortcut.brief: delete the files and trash the drive
shortcut.why: Deleted files can often be recovered, and the policy sends retired drives to IT.
shortcut.mis: Deleting files removes them for good.

proceed.text: Carry on with your regular work, since nothing here needs action.
proceed.why: Each of these situations involves confidential information in a format that needs protecting.
proceed.lesson: Protect confidential information on paper, screens and in conversation alike.

generic.text: Ask {coworker2} what they usually do and copy that.
generic.why: A coworker's habit is not the written guide, and it may be out of date.
generic.mis: Common practice is the same as the rule.

generic.text: Wait until {lead|the} brings it up before you act.
generic.why: The guide applies to you now, and waiting leaves the problem in place.
generic.mis: Someone else will raise it if it matters.

overcaution.text: Stop handling all paper and electronic files until {lead|the} reviews the whole policy with you.
overcaution.why: The concern is specific. Stopping everything delays work the policy allows.
overcaution.mis: Any rule question means stopping all handling.

setup: Customer paper files must be sent to another branch.

steps.text: Gather the files that must go
Seal them in a labeled envelope
Hand the envelope to the courier

rel: You need the files before you can seal them.
Hand over the envelope only once it is sealed.
The note lists what you gathered.
process.lesson: Gather, seal and label, hand over, and keep a note.

title: Information protection reminders
intro: You are checking a reminder sheet before it is posted by the copier.
prompt: Which line gives advice that breaks the policy?
doc.lesson: Protect confidential information on paper, on screens and in conversation.

lines.text: Erase whiteboards that show customer information before you leave.

bad.text: Leave customer information on the whiteboard if only staff use the room.
bad.why: Visitors and cleaners also use the room, so the board is erased.

lines.text: Talk about customer accounts only where nobody can overhear.

bad.text: Talk about customer accounts anywhere if you keep your voice low.
bad.why: A low voice can still be overheard, so the call moves to a private area.

lines.text: Send paper files only in sealed, labeled envelopes.

bad.text: Send paper files in an open folder when the other branch is waiting.
bad.why: Open folders can lose pages or be read in transit.

lines.text: Give old storage devices to IT to be wiped.
lines.fine: Makes sure nothing can be recovered.

review.notes: Each rule is stated as this workplace's policy; no statute is cited. Tiers: visible information, overheard talk, personal devices, files in transit, retired storage.
